title: Fontaine–Mazur modularity at the prime 2
main_claim: Every continuous, irreducible, odd 2-adic representation r: G_Q → GL_2(Qbar_2) that is unramified outside finitely many primes and de Rham at 2 with distinct Hodge–Tate weights is a Tate twist of the Galois representation of a classical cuspidal eigenform. There is no residual-image hypothesis.

issues.location: classicality.tex, Lemma ordinary-character-family (2) / Theorem potential-promodularity (family form)
issues.description: The occurrence step for the whole ordinary family over F, with the invariant-line character recorded, uses the 'more generally' family clause of the potential pro-modularity theorem. That clause is stated for framed deformation families. Applying it to a family that also records a local line is justified only in one sentence: apply the theorem to an unrestricted component that contains the family. This is plausible because support containment is set-theoretic, but it depends on the deep propagation and connectedness machinery, which I did not fully verify.
issues.evidence: 'Theorem~\ref{thm:potential-promodularity}, applied to an unrestricted framed component containing this family, gives one common F and one tame level with the asserted trace support.'

issues.description: The argument relies on an external result, Thorne2026 Theorem D: ordinary potentially crystalline representations with weights {0,1} are modular at every prime with no residual hypothesis. I could not check its exact hypotheses or its Hodge–Tate sign convention. I verified that the dualized shape (unramified sub, eps^{-1} times finite-order quotient) matches the geometric H^1 convention, and that modularity is insensitive to dualization up to twist.
issues.evidence: 'All the hypotheses of \cite[Theorem~D]{Thorne2026} are now satisfied.'

coverage:
I read in full: the introduction, the preliminaries (including the virtually solvable reduction), all of Section 8 (classicality and descent), the relative presentation proposition and its line-chart corollary, the start of the connectedness section (modular seed, transverse-chart dimension lemma), and the closing degree inequalities of the fields section. Checks I carried out:
- Bloch–Kato H^1_g computation for the higher-line lemma.
- Dimension count 5+2-3 for the ordinary family; the Euler-characteristic derivation of g-r ≥ 3-6m-h^0.
- Degree inequalities against the reducible-locus bounds.
- Finite joint-image argument.
- Construction of the eta_1(5)=c·zeta weights and the ratio eps·xi; the normalizing character lambda; oddness after the twist.
- Inducing-order bookkeeping: only the favorable order's lower-disk vector has a unit U-eigenvalue at the weight-2 points.
- Lower-disk U-eigenvalue = delta_2(2).
- With sympy: the Gauss/U-improvement matrix identities (eq. U-upper-improvement, polynomial-Gauss), plus the Gauss decomposition used in the polynomial-orbit lemma.
- The exponent inequality e2-e1 = a-b-1 ≥ 0.
- The Eisenstein-difference seed's constant-term factor.
- Cyclic descent with character correction.
I only skimmed the propagation/patching sections (deformation curve completion, completed forms/block comparison, patching) and the Selmer field construction. They are long and depend on cited results (BIP, Paškūnas–Tung, Pan) that I could not check in the time available.
sibling_notes: The family-010 board was empty when I started. The OAI H10Q paper (Section 4) cites this theorem as its weight-two modularity input. The dependence runs one way, so it is not circular.
